title: Impact of a Primary Care Gatekeeping System on Vaccination Uptake
summary:
A mandatory primary care system is currently being discussed in Germany. Under this model, general practitioners (GPs) would become the first point of contact for patients and coordinate their healthcare. At the same time, vaccination coverage among adults remains below recommended levels for many vaccines.

The aim of this study is to investigate how a mandatory primary care system should be designed to improve adult vaccination uptake. First, experts from different sectors of the German healthcare system will be interviewed regarding the potential advantages and disadvantages of such a system and possible measures to promote vaccination. Subsequently, a nationwide survey of office-based general practitioners will assess their views on different organizational, structural, and reimbursement-related features of a mandatory primary care system.

The findings will provide scientific evidence to inform the future design of a mandatory primary care system in Germany and identify strategies that may help improve adult vaccination coverage.
